concept_purpose: Lamarre coined platformativity (a performativity via platforms) to capture the infra-individual interactions between platform and human and to challenge media studies' treatment of regions as passive while overstating platforms' dynamism.
paper_title: Reformatting the stream: platformativity and the collapse of platform-area borders
paper_argument: Applies Lamarre's platformativity to streaming media to argue that the feel of platforms plays with and against received geopolitical forms, theorizing how streaming collapses borders between platform and area/region.

concept_purpose: Derrida coined hauntology in Spectres of Marx (1994) to describe how the present is perpetually haunted by unresolved ghosts of the past and unrealized futures, displacing ontology with a logic of spectral return.
paper_title: The hauntological essay film: navigating historical memory and collective trauma in The Image You Missed
paper_argument: Reads Donal Foreman's essay film The Image You Missed (about the filmmaker's father and Northern Ireland's Troubles) as a hauntological essay film that navigates collective trauma and historical memory through spectral, archival returns.

concept_purpose: Derrida's Nuclear Criticism (No Apocalypse, Not Now, 1984) theorizes nuclear war as a fabulously textual event that, being unprecedented and total, can only be anticipated rhetorically and never represented or survived as referent.
paper_title: (Un)moving images of the Third World War: nuclear narrative and nuclear aesthetic of Chris Marker's La Jetee
paper_argument: Argues Chris Marker's La Jetee (1962) exposes the Faustian terms of Gaullist France's nuclear program and, through its photo-roman aesthetic, both pre-empts and circumnavigates Derrida's claim about the impossibility of representing nuclear apocalypse.

concept_purpose: Wong proposes polylocality to conceptualize the incommensurable, messy entanglements of queer temporality, postmodern spatiality and urbanism in Asian media, against the lingering Eurocentrism of queer TV studies.
paper_title: Queering BL televisuality across Asia: queer polylocality across Thailand, Hong Kong and South Korea
paper_argument: Uses polylocality to compare a 2022 Thai BL series and a 2022 Korean BL vampire series, arguing the framework captures the transregional, heterogeneous time-space of queer (post)modernity in Asian Boys' Love television.

concept_purpose: Brooks's melodramatic mode (The Melodramatic Imagination) theorizes melodrama not as a genre but as a post-sacred mode of excess and moral legibility that dramatizes hidden ethical forces in a secular world.
paper_title: Registers of the melodramatic mode: the 1980s heroic bloodshed cycle in the history of the Hong Kong crime film
paper_argument: Argues the 1980s Hong Kong heroic bloodshed cycle operates across different registers of the melodramatic mode: melodrama (A Better Tomorrow), realism (Law with Two Phases) and modernism (City on Fire).

concept_purpose: Elsaesser theorized cinephilia as an affective, memory-laden relation to film marked by repetition, belatedness and the second viewing, reshaped by new media technologies.
paper_title: 'If I can change': multigenerational cinematic franchises, retconning, and the spectre of Rocky IV
paper_argument: Modifies Elsaesser's theories of cinephilia (for streaming-era viewing) to analyze retconning in the Rocky franchise and the 2021 re-edit Rocky IV: Rocky vs. Drago.

concept_purpose: Ostrom theorized the commons (Governing the Commons) as shared resources sustainably self-governed by communities, countering the tragedy of the commons assumption that shared resources inevitably collapse without private or state control.
paper_title: Contesting screens of energy: Gaia, the commons and infrastructure
paper_argument: Reads two Japanese documentaries (The Message of Gaia, Silent Revolution) as contested socio-ecological visions of energy, mobilizing the commons to position community-managed energy infrastructure as a site of anti-extractive collective governance.

concept_purpose: Sconce coined smart film/smart cinema (Screen, 2002) to name a post-1990s mode of ironic, blank, tonally detached art cinema positioned between Hollywood and the avant-garde.
paper_title: A blockbuster art film for the neoliberal age: blank style and 'smart' aesthetics in Maren Ade's screwball tragedy Toni Erdmann
paper_argument: Reads Maren Ade's Toni Erdmann (2016) as a screwball tragedy whose blank style and smart aesthetics formally register neoliberal precarity and the global economy's reshaping of psychic and social life.

concept_purpose: Sohn-Rethel's real abstraction (Intellectual and Manual Labour) argues that abstract conceptual thought derives historically from the material abstraction performed in commodity exchange, not from pure cognition.
paper_title: (Im)material abstractions: visions of cryptocurrency in Ivar Veermae's The Flood (2018)
paper_argument: Reads Ivar Veermae's installation The Flood (on an Estonian oil-shale mine/power plant) through Marx and Sohn-Rethel's real abstraction to argue cryptocurrency forces a rethinking of the real via its simultaneous immateriality and material extractive localization.

concept_purpose: Gomez-Barris (The Extractive Zone) theorizes extractivism and the extractive view as a colonial-capitalist mode of perceiving land and peoples as exploitable resources, against which she posits Indigenous submerged perspectives.
paper_title: Disorienting cinema: sensing beyond extractivism in the Peruvian Amazon
paper_argument: Reads Rio verde: el tiempo de los yakurunas (Sarmiento, 2017), set in an Indigenous Amazonian community, as a disorienting cinema that produces sensory modes of perception resisting extractivist logics.

concept_purpose: Visibility politics (in Mirzoeff's right-to-look lineage) names how being rendered visible to representation and surveillance is simultaneously a claim to recognition and a vector of control, explaining why the demand for representation can trap marginalized groups in the apparatus that subjugates them.
paper_title: Speculating in Latent Space: Visibility Politics and the Impasse of Representation in Generative AI
paper_argument: Through close reading of text-to-image programs, argues that generative AI operates on a gap between human and machine perception that forecloses identity-based representational speculation, marking an impasse for marginalized visibility politics.

concept_purpose: Russell coined glitch feminism to reframe the digital error/malfunction as a refusal of the binary, normative body, a productive break that opens space for Black, queer and minoritarian self-fashioning beyond fixed representational categories.
paper_title: Speculating in Latent Space: Visibility Politics and the Impasse of Representation in Generative AI
paper_argument: Turns to glitch to show how generative AI might foster a revised speculation for a marginalized political imagination attentive to the nonvisual, minoritarian experience that subtends the digital image.

concept_purpose: Chion theorized the acousmatic voice/acousmetre (building on Pierre Schaeffer) to explain how cinema mobilizes the gap between visible source and audible sound to produce power, mystery and the de-essentializing of who owns a voice.
paper_title: FKA twigs and the Impossibly Sonorous Body
paper_argument: Analyzes FKA twigs's music videos, arguing her staging of Black masochistic desire transforms the acousmatic into an impossibly sonorous entanglement that challenges the visual and sonic color line.

concept_purpose: Chion theorized the acousmatic voice/acousmetre (building on Pierre Schaeffer) to explain how the gap between visible body and audible voice can de-essentialize the link between sound, race and identity.
paper_title: The Affordances of the Acousmatic: Questioning Argentineness in El futuro perfecto
paper_argument: Argues El futuro perfecto (Nele Wohlatz, 2016) makes nearly all Argentine characters acousmatic to undo the essentializing links between sound, race and nationality.

concept_purpose: Wilderson's Afro-pessimism adapts Orlando Patterson's social death to argue that Blackness occupies a structural position of the Slave (natal alienation, dishonor, gratuitous violence) that grounds, rather than is an exception to, the modern world order.
paper_title: On Failing to Get Out
paper_argument: Reading Jordan Peele's Get Out, yokes horror to the slave narrative and the psychoanalytics of spectatorship, arguing the film stages a subject split of irresistible collusion between protagonist and antagonist rather than clean resistance.

concept_purpose: Hartman coined the afterlife of slavery to name how slavery's racialized regimes of property, dispossession and premature death persist into the present, structuring Black life long after formal abolition.
paper_title: Material Afterlives: The Quilted Poetics of Daughters of the Dust (1991) and Lemonade (2016)
paper_argument: Reads the intertextual quilted poetics linking Julie Dash's Daughters of the Dust and Beyonce's Lemonade, arguing both confront the material legacies of racialized exploitation and reproduce Black women's diasporic genealogies.

concept_purpose: Foucault's heterotopia theorizes space as socially produced and politically charged, sites that mirror, contest or invert the dominant order, rather than as a neutral container for events.
paper_title: Vicissitudes of the Underworld: Spatiality and Political Discourse in Hong Kong Gangster Films
paper_argument: Through the Infernal Affairs trilogy, the Election series and Trivisa, argues that Hong Kong gangster films use spatiality to construct an implicit political discourse about the city across two decades.

concept_purpose: Foucault's biopolitics names the modern state's power over life (the regulation of bodies, reproduction and sexuality), explaining how legal constructions of privacy and the home operate to govern female sexuality.
paper_title: Enter Your Chambers and Shut Your Doors behind You: Bodily Containment, Proliferation, and the Right to Privacy in American Law and Gothic Horror
paper_argument: Argues U.S. privacy/birth-control rulings cast the home as a safe container for female sexuality, while Gothic-horror films (The Birds, Night of the Living Dead) render the inside/outside boundary artificial and porous.

concept_purpose: Berlant theorized precarity to name the eroded sense of stability and affective exhaustion produced when neoliberal capitalism withdraws guarantees of the good life from ordinary subjects.
paper_title: Precarious Hours: Contingency and the Temporality of Live Streaming
paper_argument: Analyzing three documentaries about Chinese live streamers, argues streamers try to entrepreneurialize time but get stuck in a protracted present, binding live streaming's appeal to lived conditions of precarity displayed on screen.

concept_purpose: Doane theorized cinematic contingency to explain how modern media capture and structure the unpredictable, fleeting, non-repeatable moment, organizing the experience of time and the present.
paper_title: Precarious Hours: Contingency and the Temporality of Live Streaming
paper_argument: Uses contingency to characterize the temporal experience of live streaming (the lure of what might happen in real time) and connects that temporality to streamers' precarious labor.

concept_purpose: Glissant coined opacity (the right to opacity) to defend the colonized/racialized other's right not to be made fully transparent or knowable, refusing the demand that comprehension be a precondition of coexistence.
paper_title: Forever Opaque: Glissant, Laplanche, and Return to Seoul
paper_argument: Reading Davy Chou's Return to Seoul (2022), a portrait of a Korean-French adoptee, argues the film stages opacity against the desire to render self and other transparent, modeling living alongside one another without mastery.

concept_purpose: Laplanche theorized the enigmatic signifier/message to explain how the unconscious is formed by messages from the other that the subject can never fully decode, founding a self opaque even to itself.
paper_title: Forever Opaque: Glissant, Laplanche, and Return to Seoul
paper_argument: Pairs the enigmatic signifier with Glissant's opacity to read the adoptee protagonist's self-estrangement in Return to Seoul, arguing the film questions the fiction of a self transparent to itself.

concept_purpose: Nichols theorized documentary modes (including the observational mode) to distinguish how nonfiction films position the viewer and make truth-claims, with the observational mode withholding commentary to imply unmediated access to events.
paper_title: Feminist Observation: The Case of Un processo per stupro (A Trial for Rape, 1979)
paper_argument: Reading the 1979 Italian collective video of a gang-rape trial broadcast on RAI 2, argues the feminist filmmakers adopted the observational mode (rather than 1970s feminism's intimacy) to contest sexual violence in the legal system.

concept_purpose: Trans of color critique extends Roderick Ferguson's queer of color critique to analyze how racialized and gendered logics jointly govern bodies, here applied to how visual/computational technologies inherit medical regimes of surveillance.
paper_title: How the Computer Taught Us to See
paper_argument: Placing computer history (Xerox GUIs), medical history (DSM revisions) and queer/trans history side by side (1973-1981), argues that screen-based computer vision recapitulated the racialized and gendered logics of medical surveillance.

concept_purpose: Best and Marcus proposed surface reading as a method that attends to what is manifest on a text's surface rather than excavating hidden depths, resisting the suspicious hermeneutics of symptomatic reading.
paper_title: Just Be There: Ethics and Aesthetics of the Surface in Mike Mills's 20th Century Women
paper_argument: Reading Mike Mills's 20th Century Women (2016), argues the film enacts surface reading, recuperating the surface as a zone of lasting mystery and an ethics of openness that refuses appropriative knowledge.

concept_purpose: Rich coined compulsory heterosexuality to name how heterosexuality is socially enforced as the default; asexuality studies extends this to compulsory sexuality, the assumption that everyone is or should be sexual.
paper_title: Aromantic Comedy: The Aro/Ace Aesthetics of Together Together
paper_argument: Reading the surrogacy comedy Together Together (2021), argues its focus on a platonic, nonsexual, intergenerational friendship challenges compulsory sexuality and shows asexuality studies as fertile ground for feminist film studies.

concept_purpose: Mbembe coined necropolitics to describe sovereignty exercised as the power to dictate who may live and who must die, designating populations as disposable in the service of capital and the state.
paper_title: Castle & Crook: Necroliberalism and Cartographies of Abandonment in Maquilapolis and Senorita Extraviada
paper_argument: Reading the documentaries Maquilapolis (2006) and Senorita Extraviada (2001), argues both map the necropolitical spatial logics of post-NAFTA neoliberal modernization on the US-Mexico border, coining necroliberalism.

concept_purpose: Tuck called for desire-based research to replace damage-centered framings of Indigenous and marginalized communities, foregrounding complexity, hope and survivance rather than reducing people to brokenness.
paper_title: Reading Border through Desire: Queer Indigenous Theory, Nordic Settler Colonialism, and Trans Aesthetics
paper_argument: Reading Ali Abbasi's Border (2018) about gender-fluid trolls, uses Tuck's desire-based research plus queer Indigenous theory to argue the film can sensitize viewers to gender variance and to the Nordic settler-colonial trauma of the Sami.

concept_purpose: Berlant theorized the impasse as the stretched-out, suspended present in which subjects tread water amid attrition, a holding pattern produced when the fantasy of forward-moving good-life progress breaks down.
paper_title: Surviving the Reset: Speedrunning Spyro, Trans Mundanity, and Playing in the Impasse
paper_argument: Through autoethnography of speedrunning Spyro while transitioning, argues both videogame play and trans life are lived in Berlant's impasse, defined by prolonged waiting and negative affects like boredom and frustration.

concept_purpose: Jacobson coins the downstream as a formal-aesthetic category to name how a film can deliver ecological critique not through plot but through audio-visual technique that makes viewers perceptually trace cascading effects of human action.
paper_title: Evil Does Not Exist: Downstream Environmental Form
paper_argument: Reading Ryusuke Hamaguchi's Evil Does Not Exist (2023), argues the film turns a familiar eco-parable into a perception-challenging experience of aesthetic ambiguity, delivering a message about environmental precarity through formal downstream effects.

concept_purpose: Schwartz developed Internal Family Systems to model the mind as autonomous, interconnected parts governed by a core Self, arguing there are no bad parts and that mental health comes from compassionately integrating one's emotional sub-personalities.
paper_title: No Bad Parts: Forms of Self-Compassion in Inside Out 2
paper_argument: Argues Inside Out 2 (2024) translates mindfulness, holistic medicine and the IFS model into form, presenting emotions as autonomous-but-interconnected parts and modeling an affective life premised on rejecting emotional denial.

concept_purpose: Cavell theorized skepticism (doubt about whether we can know other minds) and argued Hollywood comedies of remarriage stage its overcoming through conversation and mutual acknowledgment, making film a site of moral philosophy.
paper_title: Suspicious Minds and Dead Bodies: Queer Romance and Skepticism in Rose Glass's Love Lies Bleeding
paper_argument: Reads Rose Glass's Love Lies Bleeding (2024) through Cavell, arguing the queer thriller opens a critical space in which doubt and insecurity between lovers are worked through toward Cavellian mutual acknowledgment.

concept_purpose: Pasolini coined the cinema of poetry to describe filmmaking that moves beyond prose-like narrative realism toward a subjective, poetic, image-driven language (the free indirect point-of-view shot) expressing the filmmaker's vision through stylistic excess.
paper_title: Alice Rohrwacher's Cinema of Poetry
paper_argument: Reading Rohrwacher's La Chimera (2023), argues Pasolini's films and writings are critical for understanding how Rohrwacher uses visual art and moves beyond realism into a poetic register.

concept_purpose: Star's ethnography of infrastructure argues that infrastructures are the normally invisible, boring sociotechnical relations that sustain practices, a lens for treating cultural practice as material, networked and political.
paper_title: Cinephile Culture as Infrastructure: Relations and Networks in Hong Kong, 1960s-1980s
paper_argument: Drawing on critical infrastructure studies, argues Hong Kong's mid-century cinephile culture (cineclubs, criticism, experimental film networks) should be read as an infrastructure of relations cultivating alternative mediascapes under colonial governance.

concept_purpose: t4t (trans-for-trans) names a trans-centric ethos of love, care and solidarity, theorized in trans studies to describe how trans people orient toward one another for safety, recognition and mutual world-making rather than toward cisnormative recognition.
paper_title: Orlando, Desire Lines: In Search of a t4t Documentary Practice
paper_argument: Argues recent trans documentaries (Preciado's Orlando, My Political Biography and Rosskam's Desire Lines) move beyond representation toward a t4t documentary practice that resists conventional form to deliver care to trans audiences.

concept_purpose: Degh and Vazsonyi coined ostension (1983) to describe how people pattern real-life behavior on shared legend models, performing or enacting legends rather than just telling them, explaining the porous boundary between folklore and lived action.
paper_title: The Surprising Folklore of Analog Horror
paper_argument: Argues the YouTube/TikTok subgenre analog horror (e.g. Kris Straub's Local 58) functions like contemporary folklore, performing the social functions of legend through ostension and legend-tripping logics.

concept_purpose: Malabou developed plasticity, the dual capacity to both receive and give form (and to explode form), to theorize how living matter and the self are open to transformation rather than fixed.
paper_title: Plastic Flesh and the Biological Oeuvre
paper_argument: Reads the bio-art of Lynn Hershman Leeson, Anicka Yi and Juliana Huxtable as exposing the plasticity of living biology, arguing biotechnology's apparent mastery over life is undone by that plasticity and troubles the human/non-human distinction.

concept_purpose: Bataille's base materialism and economy of expenditure theorize matter and affect operating below idealist visual/rational form, energies of attraction and repulsion irreducible to ideal order.
paper_title: Visceral Economies, Queer Dialectics: Eisenstein Meets Bataille
paper_argument: Maps the 1930 Paris encounter of Eisenstein and Bataille, arguing both share a cannibalistic and visceral model of mimesis constituting a visceral economy that administers affect as an aesthetic resource, and that Eisenstein embraced a queer dialectics.

concept_purpose: Bataille's informe and expenditure name an anti-idealist materialism; here invoked alongside Annette Michelson's countervailing principle that theory should not be imposed a priori on artworks.
paper_title: Bataille and Eisenstein: In Defense of Michelson's View
paper_argument: A direct rebuttal to Vogman (No. 188): argues there is no real affinity between Eisenstein's and Bataille's thought and that Bataille's concepts should not be applied top-down to Eisenstein's films, defending Michelson's view.

concept_purpose: Pavlov's reflex conditioning explained behavior as physiologically determined stimulus-response, which 1920s Soviet thinkers generalized into a materialist theory of how art conditions its audience.
paper_title: The Reflex Republic: Physiologies of Art in the Early Soviet Union
paper_argument: Recovers the 1920s reflexology of art that applied Pavlovian physiology to drama, cinema and literature (Meyerhold, Eisenstein, Tret'iakov), aiming to mold atomized individual subjectivities into a corporeal collective.

concept_purpose: Maturana and Varela coined autopoiesis to name a system that continuously produces and maintains itself through its own recursive operations.
paper_title: Cycle and Citation: What Hanne Darboven Calls Thinking
paper_argument: Reads Hanne Darboven's numerical paper machines as self-organizing, autopoietic systems, reframing Constructivism in her work and tracing El Lissitzky's influence.

concept_purpose: The counterpublic names alternative discursive arenas formed by subordinated groups against a dominant bourgeois public sphere, theorizing how excluded voices circulate critique.
paper_title: Counterpublics in Search of Infrastructures: Lessons from German Anti-Antisemitism
paper_argument: Analyzes new forms of counterpublicness on social media and in art/academic groupings amid the suppression of criticism of Zionism in Germany, using historical theories of the counterpublic to read contemporary public-sphere infrastructure.

concept_purpose: Nixon coined slow violence for harm that is gradual, attritional and dispersed across time and out of sight (e.g. environmental/structural damage), as opposed to spectacular, instantaneous violence.
paper_title: On Indiana: A Disorientation Guide
paper_argument: Critiques the artworld's at-risk discourse for fixating on acute crisis while ignoring the slow violence of colonial, anti-Black and neoliberal museum/university funding and lawfare, arguing the artworld is itself a riskocracy.

concept_purpose: Toscano coined late fascism (echoing late capitalism) to theorize fascism not as a fixed interwar type but as a recurring, plural formation entangled with race, colonialism, capitalism and crisis.
paper_title: Six Propositions After Trump's Second Victory
paper_authors: David Joselit and Pamela M. Lee
paper_argument: Reading Trump's 2024 Madison Square Garden rally against the German American Bund's 1939 Pro American Rally in the same arena, mobilize lateness/late fascism to argue the US ignores fascism's homegrown nativist history at its peril.

concept_purpose: Wollheim coined twofoldness to describe how seeing a picture involves simultaneously seeing the marked surface and the depicted object, one doubled perceptual experience.
paper_title: Surface, Material Bodies, and the Avant-Garde in Philosophy of Film
paper_argument: Reads avant-garde cinema and Annette Michelson's film criticism through Wollheim's twofoldness, arguing both understand their medium as a site of doubled perception and both recur to Kleinian ideas of infancy and the body to ground filmic materiality.

concept_purpose: Schafer's soundscape/schizophonia frame hearing as the sense best able to disclose one's embodied relation to the sonic environment, and name the modern severing of sounds from their sources.
paper_title: Ears in the Cloud: Fantasies of Networked Perception
paper_argument: Reads Christina Kubisch's installation Cloud (2017) and her Electrical Walks within the Cage/Schafer tradition, as exemplifying a tendency to credit hearing with the power to apprehend invisible network infrastructure.

concept_purpose: Bowlby coined 'attachment' and 'internal working models' to explain how the infant-caregiver bond forms enduring mental templates governing later emotional and social development
paper_title: Attachment Theory and Mentalization in Richard Linklater's Boyhood
paper_argument: Argues that Boyhood's classroom scenes overtly stage Bowlby's developmental paradigm, using attachment research's empirical apparatus to dramatize cinematic character development across the lifespan

concept_purpose: Fonagy developed 'mentalization' (reflective functioning) to describe the capacity to understand oneself and others in terms of mental states, rooted in secure attachment
paper_title: Attachment Theory and Mentalization in Richard Linklater's Boyhood
paper_argument: Contends that Linklater implicitly and perhaps unconsciously leans on Fonagy's mentalization model in the transitions between scenes to convey interior development

concept_purpose: Winnicott coined the 'transitional object' and 'transitional space' to theorize the intermediate area of experience between inner reality and the external world, the seat of play and culture
paper_title: The Representation of Holocaust Trauma in The Song of Terezin by Franz Waxman: A Psychoanalytic Listening
paper_argument: Uses transitional space to argue that Waxman's musical memorial opens an ethical, intermediate zone where listeners can encounter the trauma of the Other through attentive (psychoanalytic) listening

concept_purpose: Cultural trauma theory explains how collective catastrophes are non-verbally and belatedly registered and transmitted, exceeding ordinary representation
paper_title: The Representation of Holocaust Trauma in The Song of Terezin by Franz Waxman: A Psychoanalytic Listening
paper_argument: Argues that music, through its affective and bodily means, constructs a discourse of Holocaust trauma and mourning that words cannot, making The Song of Terezin a sonic mechanism of cultural memory

concept_purpose: Freud's 'the uncanny' (das Unheimliche) names the disturbing return of the familiar made strange, tied to repression and the death drive
paper_title: Whistler's Mothers: Painters, Models, and Uncanny Arrangements
paper_argument: Reads Whistler's maternal portraiture through the Freudian uncanny to analyze the unsettling psychic arrangements between painter, model and viewer

keyword: spectacular silence / sonic economy of moviegoing
theorist: Carlo Cenciarelli (building on cinema sound studies)
concept_purpose: The notion of 'spectacular silence' is advanced to explain a shift in how silence (vs. loudness) is marketed as the unique value of the cinematic listening experience
paper_title: Spectacular Silence and the Ends of Moviegoing: The Cinema as A Quiet Place (c. 2021)
journal: Music, Sound, and the Moving Image
paper_argument: Argues that the A Quiet Place franchise's reversed sonic economy, foregrounding silence over spectacular sound, marks a broader transformation in the meanings and values of cinema as a place for listening after COVID-19 closures

concept_purpose: Turner adapted van Gennep's rites-of-passage 'liminality' to theorize the ambiguous, in-between, threshold state that suspends ordinary social structure
paper_title: Ambiguity and Liminality as Sonic Strategies in The Bridge
journal: Music, Sound, and the Moving Image
paper_argument: Argues that The Bridge's soundtrack consciously breaks conventional boundaries of music and sound design to create a liminal, ambiguous atmosphere mirroring the series' border setting and the 'gaps' between people

concept_purpose: Kristeva theorized 'abjection' as the visceral horror at the breakdown of meaning and the self-other boundary, explaining attraction-repulsion toward the impure
paper_title: Blood as a Fashion Statement: On the Trend of 'Abjection Chic' in Contemporary Horror Cinema
paper_argument: Coins 'abjection chic' to argue that films like Last Night in Soho and Men evoke abject cult-horror conventions only to disembody and aestheticize them, neutralizing the subversive potential of cinematic abjection

concept_purpose: Williams coined the 'body genres' (horror, melodrama, pornography) to explain how excessive bodily affect is culturally dismissed yet central to these forms' appeal
paper_title: Blood as a Fashion Statement: On the Trend of 'Abjection Chic' in Contemporary Horror Cinema
paper_argument: Draws on Williams's body genres to situate horror's sensory excess as the very quality that 'abjection chic' suppresses in pursuit of mainstream respectability and cultural capital

concept_purpose: Chion theorized the cinematic voice and 'voco-centrism' to explain how the human voice instantly establishes a hierarchy of perception in the soundtrack
paper_title: The Voice of Meiko Kaji in 1970s Japanese Exploitation Cinema
paper_argument: Uses Chion's voco-centrism to argue that Kaji's sung theme songs dominate the soundscape and carry her characters' feminist vengeance, transforming silence and song into a vehicle of agency in exploitation cinema

concept_purpose: Eisenstein coined 'plasmaticness' in his Disney writings to name animation's primal, revolutionary rejection of fixed form through endless metamorphosis
paper_title: Posthumous Portraits in Motion: Experimental Animation, Metamorphosis and Reflections on Mortality
paper_argument: Uses paint-on-glass metamorphic animation of unclaimed deceased to argue metamorphosis is a self-referential engagement with animation's plasmatic, contradictory life-giving and destructive capacities, confronting mortality and the ethics of representing the dead

concept_purpose: Husserl's transcendental phenomenology brackets the natural attitude to study the structures of consciousness as they appear, here adapted to the lived act of animating
paper_title: The Phenomenology of Animation
paper_argument: Argues for a 'pure' phenomenology of animation centered on the animator's performative creation of the frame, distinguishing it from Sobchack's projection-focused film phenomenology

concept_purpose: Goethe's morphology theorized organic form as continuous transformation and development, used to explain why metamorphosis is treated as constitutive of animation
paper_title: Animating Goethe
paper_argument: Argues the claim that metamorphosis is inherent to animation neglects Goethean morphology, reconstructing its lineage through Eisenstein, Bazin and others

concept_purpose: The 'useful cinema' framework was coined to study non-theatrical, instrumental moving images made to do work within institutions
paper_title: Useful Animation: Iconography, Infrastructure and Impact
paper_authors: Malcolm Cook; Michael Cowan; Scott Curtis
paper_argument: Extends 'useful cinema' to 'useful animation', arguing across iconography, infrastructure and knowledge that animation has historically functioned as a practical and epistemic tool in professional and institutional contexts

concept_purpose: Cholodenko framed animation as the 'illusion of life', theorizing the medium's self-conscious staging of liveliness and animatedness
paper_title: Alive and Lifelike: Theatricality and Animation
paper_argument: Uses Chuck Jones's Duck Amuck to argue animation historiography should proceed through theatricality, since animation lays bare the performed, 'alive and lifelike' theatricality underlying cinema itself

concept_purpose: Grosz's corporeal feminism reconceives the body as a fluid sexually-differentiated surface; the Deleuzo-Guattarian Body without Organs names a de-stratified body of pure intensities
paper_title: Corporeal topographies: Body-oriented art of Mona Hatoum and Amal Kenawy
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Argues Hatoum and Kenawy render female corporeality as a topographical map, showing gender as porous fluid processes co-constituted by material and sociopolitical contexts rather than a fixed essence

concept_purpose: Sobchack theorized film as an embodied, reciprocal act of perception in which film and viewer are both sensuous seeing subjects
paper_title: Film symbiosis: Embodied spectatorship and sensory (auto)ethnography in Sweetgrass
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Develops 'film symbiosis' from Sobchack's phenomenology, arguing observational and sensory-ethnographic works create an embodied, symbiotic address between spectator and the on-screen nonhuman other

concept_purpose: Bubandt's 'haunted geologies' names how disturbed, contaminated landscapes carry the spectral 'ghost strata' of ecological and historical loss in the Anthropocene
paper_title: Above and below: The sounding of haunted geologies
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Uses haunted geologies to argue field recording and sound post-production function as affective acts of divination that sonically register ghost strata at contested UK and Australian sites

concept_purpose: Anzaldua's 'borderlands' theorizes the border as a plural, unstable, embodied zone of mestiza consciousness articulating Chicana and queer in-between experience
paper_title: Towards lesbian bodylands: Refiguring lesbian communities in Brazilian cinema
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Coins 'bodylands' after Anzaldua to argue recent Brazilian films interweave the lesbian body, the filmic body and the spectator's body, resisting reductive visibility and reimagining lesbian existence through nonhuman elements

concept_purpose: Eribon's sociology of shame, the 'social verdict' and resubjectivation explains how marginalized queer subjects internalize exclusion then remake belonging through chosen bonds
paper_title: In search of the lost community: On two Central American trans films
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Draws on Eribon to argue that in two Central American trans films the protagonists reconstitute community through chosen families and everyday care, reappropriating street, bar and home against hegemonic norms

concept_purpose: Bakhtin's 'chronotope' names the intrinsic fusion of time and space in cultural forms, organizing meaning and social relations
paper_title: The chronotopes of radical film: Collective exhibition and the social practice of 'Cinema Action'
journal: MIRAJ: The Moving Image Review & Art Journal
paper_argument: Applies the chronotope to 1970s British film collectives, arguing the social spaces of itinerant production, exhibition and reception shape the politics of radical cinema and reinstate Cinema Action's historiographic significance
